messages:
lisa (customer): hey @maria — our app started seeing a bunch of 429s around 08:12 UTC and some customers are complaining about failed batches. usage didn't change on our end. any chance this is on Redwood's side? we also saw an unexpected billing spike in the dashboard :confused:

maria (support): @lisa sorry you're hitting this. can you paste a sample request id or a short repro? are the 429s returning x-rate-limit headers? we'll escalate if it's on our side. :ear:

lisa (customer): example request id: req_0a1b2c3d. headers show x-rate-limit-remaining: 0 and x-rate-limit-reset: 12 (seconds). we usually burst higher than that. here's a curl we used: 

```

curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${REDWOOD_KEY}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"open-llm-16k","prompt":"...","max_tokens":512}'

```

maria (support): thanks. escalating to eng-sre. adding all. assigning P0 due to customer impact. pinging @ajay and @kai.

ajay (eng-sre): looking now. I can see a spike of 429s from the canary cohort starting 08:10 UTC. It looks like a new rate-policy (v2) was rolled to ~10% (rp-canary-7) at 08:05 via canary. Canary ID rp-canary-7. Observability shows the per-client token-bucket burst cap decreased from 120 to 20 for the canary group. That would explain the bursts failing.

kai (eng-platform): yeah that was my canary push — we tightened the burst window to reduce tail-cost for noisy tenants. it passed unit tests but we didn't simulate multi-tenant burst patterns well. sorry folks.

ryan (support): customer impact confirmed. multiple customers in the canary cohort reporting 429 + billing surprises. we should rollback the canary now and offer credits.

ajay (eng-sre): Agreed. we should rollback immediately and confirm metrics. rollback plan: 
1) remove rp-canary-7 from traffic routing (platform CLI)
2) revert rate-policy v2 to previous burst settings for that cohort
3) monitor 429 count and latency for 30m

Commands I will run: 
```
platform-cli route set --remove-cohort rp-canary-7 --force
platform-cli ratepolicy revert --policy-id rp-v2 --to-version rp-v1 --cohort rp-canary-7
```

ops-oncall: if you run the CLI, ping me to open a deploy window in case network churn happens.

kai (eng-platform): I'm ready to run or approve. Ajay, do you want me to execute step 1 or do you have privileges?

ajay (eng-sre): I can run step 1 and 2. initiating now.

deploy-bot: Initiating workflow: remove-cohort rp-canary-7 by ajay at 2026-03-15T08:14:02Z. Status: IN_PROGRESS.

maria (support): looping back to customer: we'll reach out with ETA and a mitigation plan. offering temporary quota bump and credits while we investigate.

deploy-bot: remove-cohort rp-canary-7 completed. revert-ratepolicy rp-v2 -> rp-v1 for cohort rp-canary-7 started.

ajay (eng-sre): revert command executed. we'll now re-open routing to previous settings and trigger a config reload across edge nodes.

deploy-bot: revert-ratepolicy completed. config-reload triggered.

ops-oncall: watching metrics. initial telemetry shows 429s dropping to baseline within 60s. latency also stable.

ajay (eng-sre): can everyone confirm we see error rate back to normal? I'm seeing 429s per-min down from 1200 to 30 in the last 2 minutes in the canary cohort.

kai (eng-platform): confirm. rolling back the rollout window and marking this canary as FAILED in the rollout tracker (rt-2026-03-15). I'll also revoke the auto-schedule for any remaining cohorts until we fix the burst model.

maria (support): @lisa — we rolled back the canary (rp-canary-7) at 08:14 UTC. Can you validate on your side? we'll apply a quota bump for impacted orgs and follow up with a credit.

lisa (customer): confirmed — requests look normal again. thanks for the quick turnaround. appreciate the credit offer.

ryan (support): opened ticket RED-9842 for remediation and crediting. noting impacted org IDs: org_44, org_67, org_128. sending an initial notification to those orgs with root cause and steps.

ajay (eng-sre): postmortem action items: 
- platform: add multi-tenant burst simulation to canary test harness (kai) :hammer_and_wrench:
- runtime: introduce gradual burst throttling ramp for policies (ajay) :gear:
- support: template for rapid customer communication and credits (maria/ryan) :memo:
- infra: alert for sudden billing anomalies correlated with 429 spikes (kai/eng-sre) :rotating_light:

kai (eng-platform): timeline note: don't re-run the policy until we have synthetic tests showing <1% error delta in 30m under targeted burst shapes. I'll schedule a dry-run next week.

maria (support): thanks all. I'll follow up with the customers and close the escalations after credits applied. tagging for visibility: @ops-oncall @ajay @kai @ryan. :white_check_mark:
